The sentence establishes that you get a bicycle, not what you do with it.\']}/>\\r\\n243:      <details className=\\"cr-extension\\"><summary>More Group 2 forms, with the sentence intact</summary><p><strong>Only when</strong> and <strong>only where</strong> can restrict the occasions or places of an outcome: “The fountain runs only when its pump is on.” A running fountain requires an operating pump. The pump being on does not establish that the fountain runs.</p><p><strong>Requires</strong> directly names a requirement: “Entry requires a current pass.” Preserve current. <strong>Always</strong> needs the sentence\'s subject and scope: “The upstairs room is always quiet when the door is shut.” Here a shut door establishes quiet, not the other way around.</p><p><strong>Only</strong> and <strong>the only</strong> are different complete expressions. “Only people who get a bicycle win this raffle” and “The only people who win this raffle are people who get a bicycle” both preserve the rule: winning establishes getting a bicycle.</p></details>\\r\\n254:      <p>Starting from getting a bicycle and concluding that you win is the tempting <strong>reverse</strong>. Its condition comes last, but winning is still enough to establish getting a bicycle. That condition still goes left. Don\'t let the first phrase in English choose the first side of your diagram.</p>\\r\\n272:      <RuleDiagram left=\\"Win the raffle\\" right=\\"Get a bicycle\\"/>\\r\\n283:      <p>Now move the if-clause: “You get a bicycle if you win the raffle.” The winning condition comes last in English but still goes left in the diagram. Get bicycle means you get a bicycle. Our original is Win → Get bicycle.</p>\\r\\n289:      <p>We already know that not getting a bicycle rules out winning. Write that as <strong>~Get bicycle → ~Win</strong>. The <strong>~</strong> sign means <strong>not</strong>. Not getting the outcome is different from not having received it yet.</p>\\r\\n290:      <p>To write a contrapositive from a diagram, reverse the two sides and negate <strong>both complete conditions</strong>. A condition already containing not loses that not when we negate it. Let\'s try all four patterns.</p>\\r\\n304:        <details><summary>How should I abbreviate the conditions?</summary><p>Use short labels that bring back the complete idea. There is no fixed letter limit.</p></details>\\r\\n"}'}]

false);\\r\\n  const focusAfterClose = useRef<number | null>(null);\\r\\n  const list = useRef<HTMLOListElement>(null);\\r\\n  useEffect(() => {\\r\\n    const update = () => {\\r\\n      const width = root.current?.getBoundingClientRect().width || window.innerWidth;\\r\\n      setCompact(width <= 900);\\r\\n    };\\r\\n    update();\\r\\n    const observer = typeof ResizeObserver === \'undefined\' ? null : new ResizeObserver(update);\\r\\n    if (root.current) observer?.observe(root.current);\\r\\n    window.addEventListener(\'resize\', update);\\r\\n    return () => { observer?.disconnect(); window.removeEventListener(\'resize\', update); };\\r\\n  }, []);\\r\\n  useEffect(() => {\\r\\n    const selected = list.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(\'[aria-current=\\"page\\"]\');\\r\\n    const rail = list.current?.closest<HTMLElement>(\'.co-page-sidebar-scroll\');\\r\\n    if (!selected || !rail || compact) return;\\r\\n    const row = selected.getBoundingClientRect();\\r\\n    const viewport = rail.getBoundingClientRect();\\r\\n    if (row.top < viewport.top) rail.scrollTop -= viewport.top - row.top + 12;\\r\\n    else if (row.bottom > viewport.bottom) rail.scrollTop += row.bottom - viewport.bottom + 12;\\r\\n  }, [page, compact]);\\r\\n  function focusPage(index: number) {\\r\\n    requestAnimationFrame(() => {\\r\\n      const heading = root.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-lesson-page=\\"${index}\\"] h2`);\\r\\n      if (!heading) return;\\r\\n      heading.tabIndex = -1;\\r\\n      heading.focus({ preventScroll: true });\\r\\n      heading.closest(\'section\')?.scrollIntoView?.({ block: \'start\', behavior: \'instant\' });\\r\\n    });\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  function go(index: number) {\\r\\n    setPage(index);\\r\\n    if (compact && contents) focusAfterClose.current = index;\\r\\n    else focusPage(index);\\r\\n    setContents(false);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  const pageLinks = (desktop: boolean) => <ol ref={desktop ? list : undefined} className=\\"co-page-list\\">\\r\\n    {pages.map((item, index) => <li key={index}><button type=\\"button\\" aria-current={page === index ? \'page\' : undefined} onClick={() => go(index)}><span className=\\"co-page-number\\" aria-hidden=\\"true\\">{String(index + 1).padStart(2, \'0\')}</span><span className=\\"co-page-link-title\\">{item.title}</span>{page === index && <span className=\\"co-sr-only\\">, current page</span>}</button></li>)}\\r\\n  </ol>;\\r\\n  return <div ref={root} className=\\"co-pages cr-sequence\\" data-compact={compact}>\\r\\n    <aside className=\\"co-page-sidebar\\" hidden={compact}>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"co-page-sidebar-scroll\\">\\r\\n        <div className=\\"co-page-sidebar-heading\\"><p className=\\"co-kicker\\">Conditional logic</p><h2>In this lesson</h2><p>Page {page + 1} of {pages.length}</p></div>\\r\\n        <nav aria-label=\\"Lesson pages\\">{pageLinks(true)}</nav>\\r\\n      </div>\\r\\n    </aside>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-reading-canvas\\">\\r\\n      <div className=\\"co-page-bar\\">\\r\\n        <div><span className=\\"co-kicker\\">Page {page + 1} of {pages.length}</span><p aria-live=\\"polite\\">{pages[page].title}</p>{compact && page < pages.length - 1 && <small>Next: {pages[page + 1].title}</small>}</div>\\r\\n        {compact && <Sheet open={contents} onOpenChange={setContents}><SheetTrigger asChild><button type=\\"button\\">Lesson pages <span aria-hidden=\\"true\\">☰</span></button></SheetTrigger><SheetContent side=\\"left\\" className=\\"co-mobile-page-drawer\\" onCloseAutoFocus={event => {\\r\\n          if (focusAfterClose.current !== null) {\\r\\n            event.preventDefault();\\r\\n            focusPage(focusAfterClose.current);\\r\\n            focusAfterClose.current = null;\\r\\n          }\\r\\n        }}><SheetTitle>In this lesson</SheetTitle><SheetDescription>Page {page + 1} of {pages.length}. Choose a page to read.</SheetDescription><nav aria-label=\\"Lesson pages\\">{pageLinks(false)}</nav></SheetContent></Sheet>}\\r\\n        <div className=\\"co-page-track\\" aria-hidden=\\"true\\"><span style={{ transform: `scaleX(${(page + 1) / pages.length})` }}/></div>\\r\\n      </div>\\r\\n    {pages.map((item, index) => <div className=\\"co-page\\" data-lesson-page={index} key={index} hidden={index !== page}>{item.content}</div>)}\\r\\n    <nav className=\\"co-page-turn\\" aria-label=\\"Reading navigation\\">\\r\\n      <button type=\\"button\\" disabled={page === 0} onClick={() => go(page - 1)}><span aria-hidden=\\"true\\">←</span><span>Back<small>{page > 0 ? pages[page - 1].title : \'First page\'}</small></span></button>\\r\\n      {page < pages.length - 1 ? <button type=\\"button\\" className=\\"co-next-page\\" onClick={() => go(page + 1)}><span>Next<small>{pages[page + 1].title}</small></span><span aria-hidden=\\"true\\">→</span></button> : <p>You\'ve reached the end of the reading.</p>}\\r\\n    </nav>\\r\\n    {page === pages.length - 1 && children}\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  </div>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n"}'}]

## assistant

Current Intro to LR has **13 primary path actions: 8 teaching pages, 3 standalone labs, and 2 six-question practice sets**. Source: [introToLrPath.ts](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/content/introToLrPath.ts:36).

| Order | Teaching or practice |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | Three Parts → Argument → Premises → Conclusions → Five Types |
| 6 | Conclusion Type Lab |
| 7–8 | Beyond Premises and Conclusions → Two-Part Conclusion Check |
| 9 | Main Conclusion Lab |
| 10 | First-Sentence vs Rebuttal Structures |
| 11 | First-Sentence vs Rebuttal Lab |
| 12–13 | First-Sentence Main Conclusion practice → Rebuttal Main Conclusion practice |

The eight notes contain **seven answer-and-feedback widgets across four notes**:

- **Premises:** indicator classification and support-sentence check.
- **Conclusions:** indicator classification, eight-item pop quiz, conclusion selection.
- **Five Types:** five-example classification switchboard.
- **Two-Part Check:** three claims, each requiring two yes/no judgments.

Other interactions are guided demonstrations or reveals: anatomy scanner, support visualization, definition cards, hover terms, role definitions. They should not be counted as independent practice. `RoleLabeler` and `RoleSpotlightSequence` are imported but not rendered in the current notes. Evidence: [IntroLessonPage.tsx](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/modules/lessons/notes/IntroLessonPage.tsx:347).

Lab requirements differ:

- **Conclusion Type Lab:** 12 items. Pick before feedback; an incorrect response still permits advancement.
- **Main Conclusion Lab:** select and check a sentence; correct selection required to advance.
- **First-Sentence vs Rebuttal Lab:** 20 stimuli with four reasoning steps. “Skip / Reveal All” permits assisted completion.

**Next on a note records completion without requiring its embedded exercises.** Therefore, completion is not proof of mastery. [IntroNotesShell.tsx](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/modules/lessons/notes/IntroNotesShell.tsx:43)

Reference tools, flashcards, simulator routes, and the separate older workbook are excluded from these primary-path counts. Live student assignment/access was unavailable; this is verified source behavior, not a live enrollment audit.

The useful comparison is **short teaching followed by specific response-and-feedback opportunities, plus three deliberately placed practice transitions**. Intro to LR does not place a standalone drill after every teaching page.

Keep one stable progress row per user.)\\r\\nexport function progressIdFor(userId: string): string {\\r\\n  // Deterministic UUIDv5-like derivation: hash userId into a stable string.\\r\\n  // Simple FNV-1a 32-bit; collision risk is acceptable since the progress row is\\r\\n  // user-scoped (table key already partitions by user).\\r\\n  let h = 0x811c9dc5;\\r\\n  for (let i = 0; i < userId.length; i++) {\\r\\n    h ^= userId.charCodeAt(i);\\r\\n    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  const hex = (h >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, \'0\');\\r\\n  return `00000000-0000-4000-8000-${hex.padEnd(12, \'0\')}`;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function useModuleProgress(_userId?: string): {\\r\\n  progress: ModuleProgress | null;\\r\\n  loadError: string | null;\\r\\n  retryLoad: () => void;\\r\\n  markRouteVisited: (routeId: string) => Promise<void>;\\r\\n  markLessonComplete: (lessonId: string, routeId: string) => Promise<void>;\\r\\n  markDrillComplete: (drillId: string) => Promise<void>;\\r\\n  markMilestoneComplete: (milestoneId: string) => Promise<void>;\\r\\n  markHardSectionComplete: (sectionId: string) => Promise<void>;\\r\\n  markCapstoneComplete: (capstoneId: \'M1.13\' | \'M5.8\') => Promise<void>;\\r\\n} {\\r\\n  const { user: authUser } = useAuth();\\r\\n  const [storedProgress, setProgress] = useState<ModuleProgress | null>(null);\\r\\n  const progress = storedProgress?.user_id === authUser?.id ? storedProgress : null;\\r\\n  const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState<string | null>(null);\\r\\n  const [loadAttempt, setLoadAttempt] = useState(0);\\r\\n\\r\\n  useEffect(() => {\\r\\n    if (!authUser) return;\\r\\n    setLoadError(null);\\r\\n    let cancelled = false;\\r\\n    const userId = authUser.id;\\r\\n    const progressId = progressIdFor(userId);\\r\\n    (async () => {\\r\\n      try {\\r\\n        const persist = getPersistence(userId);\\r\\n        // Wait for cloud hydration before treating the row as missing, otherwise a\\r\\n        // cold cross-device load fabricates a default row and clobbers real progress.\\r\\n        await persist.ready();\\r\\n        if (cancelled) return;\\r\\n        let existing = await persist.get<ModuleProgress>(TABLES.module_progress, progressId);\\r\\n        if (!existing) {\\r\\n          existing = ModuleProgress.parse({\\r\\n            id: progressId,\\r\\n            user_id: userId,\\r\\n            unlocked_modules: [\'M1\', \'M2\', \'M3\', \'M5\', \'M6\'],\\r\\n            unlocked_routes: INITIAL_UNLOCKED_ROUTES,\\r\\n            completed_lessons: [],\\r\\n            completed_drills: [],\\r\\n            completed_milestones: [],\\r\\n            completed_hard_sections: [],\\r\\n            completed_capstones: [],\\r\\n            updated_at: now(),\\r\\n          });\\r\\n          await persist.set(TABLES.module_progress, progressId, existing);\\r\\n          existing = await persist.get<ModuleProgress>(TABLES.module_progress, progressId) ?? existing;\\r\\n        }\\r\\n        if (!cancelled) setProgress(existing);\\r\\n      } catch (e) {\\r\\n        console.error(\'[useModuleProgress] initial load failed\', {\\r\\n          userId,\\r\\n          error: e,\\r\\n        });\\r\\n        if (!cancelled) setLoadError(\'Bootcamp progress could not be confirmed in your account. Try loading it again.\');\\r\\n      }\\r\\n    })();\\r\\n    return () => {\\r\\n      cancelled = true;\\r\\n    };\\r\\n  }, [authUser, loadAttempt]);\\r\\n\\r\\n  const markRouteVisited = useCallback(async (_routeId: string) => {\\r\\n    // Reserved for analytics in Module 6.\\r\\n  }, []);\\r\\n\\r\\n  const markLessonComplete = useCallback(\\r\\n    async (lessonId: string, routeId: string) => {\\r\\n      if (!authUser) {\\r\\n        throw new Error(\'markLessonComplete called with no authenticated user\');\\r\\n      }\\r\\n      const userId = authUser.id;\\r\\n      const progressId = progressIdFor(userId);\\r\\n      const persist = getPersistence(userId);\\r\\n      try {\\r\\n        const current = await persist.get<ModuleProgress>(TABLES.module_progress, progressId);\\r\\n        const base = current ?? progress;\\r\\n        if (!base) {\\r\\n          throw new Error(\'markLessonComplete: progress not yet loaded\');\\r\\n        }\\r\\n        const completed = base.completed_lessons.includes(lessonId)\\r\\n          ? base.completed_lessons\\r\\n          : [...base.completed_lessons, lessonId];\\r\\n        const shape: ProgressShape = {\\r\\n          unlocked_routes: base.unlocked_routes,\\r\\n          completed_lessons: completed,\\r\\n          completed_drills: base.completed_drills,\\r\\n        };\\r\\n        const additions = unlockNext(routeId, shape);\\r\\n        const merged: ModuleProgress = {\\r\\n          ...base,\\r\\n          completed_lessons: completed,\\r\\n          unlocked_routes: Array.from(new Set([...base.unlocked_routes, ...additions])),\\r\\n          updated_at: now(),\\r\\n        };\\r\\n        await persist.set(TABLES.module_progress, progressId, merged);\\r\\n        setProgress(await persist.get<ModuleProgress>(TABLES.module_progress, progressId) ?? className=\\"cr-sequence\\">\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={1} label=\\"Start with meaning\\" title=\\"What does a conditional tell you?\\">\\r\\n      <p>A <strong>condition</strong> is an idea that You win a raffle. You get a bicycle. We can ask whether either condition holds in a particular case.</p>\\r\\n      <p>A <strong>conditional statement</strong> tells us that if one condition is true, another has to be true too. Borrowing goes left; having a key goes right.\', \'Having a key is required for borrowing. Only if appears in the middle, but it still identifies the necessary condition.\']}/>\\r\\n      <h3>The indicator can also follow its target</h3>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-language-pair\\"><p>[Having a key] is <strong>required</strong> for borrowing a locker.</p><p>Borrowing a locker <strong>requires</strong> [having a key].</p><span>Having a key is the requirement in both sentences.</span></div>\\r\\n      <p>The target is the complete idea the indicator refers to. It comes before required in the first sentence and after requires in the second. Having a key still goes right. We find it by asking what is required, not by taking whichever words come next.</p>\\r\\n      <p>You\'ll work through the less familiar expressions in their Group 1 and Group 2 lessons. For each one, keep the whole sentence: what is enough, and what does it require?</p>\\r\\n      <p>Let\'s build an original diagram slowly. Choose labels you can read back.</li><li><strong>Write the contrapositive.</strong> Reverse the sides and negate both complete conditions.</li><li><strong>Read both in English.</strong> Compare them with what the original sentence actually requires.</li></ol></div>\\r\\n      <p>The original and its contrapositive describe the same relationship. If writing both helps you see that relationship, write both. If you can read the contrapositive from the original when it is relevant, you needn\'t copy it merely to have a second line.</p>\\r\\n      <p>Read an arrow forward to use its stated direction. To read its contrapositive, start from the right condition\'s absence and work back to the left condition\'s absence. That is a different move from reading the arrow backward unchanged.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={10} label=\\"Practical diagramming questions\\" title=\\"Use writing to make your reasoning easier to check\\">\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-faq\\">\\r\\n        <details><summary>When should I diagram?</summary><p>While learning, write enough to make your choices visible. A difficult sentence, several rules or a connection you keep rereading can be a reason to put the relationship on paper. With practice, you may hold a simple rule mentally. Use the writing to help the reasoning.</p></details>\\r\\n        <details><summary>How do I check whether my diagram is right?</summary><p>Read it back and compare the whole meaning. Did you keep each restriction? Does your arrow promise something the original leaves open? When a diagram is wrong, record the exact phrase and the mistake it produced. That gives you something specific to practice. Familiarity alone is not proof of correctness.</p></details>\\r\\n        <details><summary>What if writing takes time?</summary><p>Start by producing a correct, readable diagram. Speed is a later practice goal. Writing can reduce rereading, but it does not save time in every case. Compare how it helps on the sentences you are actually working through. First make the relationship accurate. Work on speed once you can explain why the arrow follows. </p></details>\\r\\n        <details><summary>Should I always write the contrapositive?</summary><p>You need to understand it every time. Write it when it helps you use the missing requirement, inspect your translation or connect rules. Otherwise, you may read that direction from the original. Extra notation should have a job.</p></details>\\r\\n        <aside className=\\"cr-training-note\\"><h3>Why this practice asks for both</h3><p>In the integrated drill, write or choose the original and the contrapositive. We\'re checking that you can produce both. Once that skill is reliable, a performance task need not require both lines for every rule.</p></aside>\\r\\n        <details><summary>How should I abbreviate the conditions?</summary><p>Use short labels that bring back the complete idea. W might mean win this raffle. Current pass may be clearer than a single letter if you\'re tracking several kinds of pass. Shortening should save writing without losing meaning. There is no fixed letter limit.</p></details>\\r\\n      </div>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Only envelopes with a paid stamp go into this tray. Someone wrote Paid stamp → In tray. What needs repairing?\\" options={[\'The labels need to be longer.\', \'The arrow makes the requirement enough.\', \'Nothing; the first phrase always goes left.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'Longer labels would not repair the direction. Let\'s inspect precisely which idea an indicator refers to.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={11} label=\\"Find the target\\" title=\\"Read the whole idea the indicator refers to\\">\\r\\n      <p>An indicator\'s <strong>target</strong> is the complete word or phrase it refers to. Read which complete idea the sentence calls required. Then give that idea its role in the diagram.</p>\\r\\n      <p>When the wording still feels uncertain, we can test a proposed translation against an imagined case.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={12} label=\\"Check an interpretation\\" title=\\"Try the sentence from the inside\\">\\r\\n      <p>A <strong>Personalized If/Then</strong> lets you test what a proposed sufficient condition would establish. First read the ordinary meaning. Propose the sufficient idea. Imagine a case meeting it. Ask what the sentence now requires.</p>\\r\\n      <blockquote>Only people wearing helmets ride the studio bikes.</blockquote><p>The sentence restricts riders to people wearing helmets. Keep that meaning while trying each proposed starting point.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-personalized\\"><div><p className=\\"co-kicker\\">First proposed starting point</p><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"If I\'m riding a studio bike, what does this sentence tell me?\\" options={[\'I am wearing a helmet.\', \'The helmet question is open.\']} correct={0} feedback={[\'The sentence puts every rider in the helmet-wearing group. If you meet the riding condition, the sentence does settle helmet wearing.\']}/></div><div><p className=\\"co-kicker\\">Try the other starting point</p><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"If I\'m wearing a helmet, must I be riding a studio bike?\\" options={[\'Yes, the helmet proves riding.\', \'No, I could wear one without riding.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You gave every helmet wearer a ride. The sentence restricts riders; it does not make all helmet wearers riders.\', \'A helmet wearer waiting beside a bike fits the sentence. Wearing helmet → Riding would add a promise the original did not make.\']}/></div></div>\\r\\n      <p>The first reading matches the sentence. The second proposed arrow fails because it rules out a case the original permits. Use the imagined situation to inspect meaning, not to supply extra facts from what usually happens.</p>\\r\\n      <h3>Use the What Test beside it</h3><p>Ask a sensible question about the expression: only what? People wearing helmets. What is required? Wearing a helmet. What is enough? Riding a studio bike, under this rule, establishes that requirement.</p>\\r\\n      <p>The What Test finds the complete target. The Personalized If/Then checks what your proposed direction says about a case. Use them together when one part of the translation is unclear.</p>\\r\\n      <p>We\'ve now read the relationship, understood its limits, written both directions and checked the language. Put those pieces together with fresh sentences.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={13} label=\\"Use the whole process\\" title=\\"Build an original and its contrapositive\\">\\r\\n      <p>For each sentence, identify the indicator and both complete conditions. Choose the original diagram, then its contrapositive. Read both back before checking.</p>\\r\\n      <p>You can look back. The job here is to produce and inspect the reasoning, not to prove you memorized every expression on the first reading. The labels below keep the complete ideas visible while you choose the directions.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-integrated-grid\\">{referencePracticeItems.map((item, index) => <IntegratedItem item={item} number={index + 1} key={item.sentence}/>)}</div>\\r\\n      <p>If an answer needs revision, name the exact issue: lost qualification, wrong role, reversed arrow or incomplete negation. Then retry that item. Your targeted Group 1 and Group 2 work gives you more practice with individual expressions; this set checks whether the steps hold together.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n    <section id=\\"reference-boundary\\" className=\\"cr-boundary co-section\\" data-reference-boundary data-toc data-toc-title=\\"Permission and instructions\\">\\r\\n      <p className=\\"co-kicker\\">Before the attached practice</p><h2>Keep what the sentence actually gives you</h2>\\r\\n      <p>The core process is now in place. One more distinction matters for the practice: a conditional can give permission or an instruction. Preserve that strength instead of turning it into a report of what someone did.</p>\\r\\n      <blockquote>Every guest with a ticket may use the cloakroom.</blockquote><p>May use gives permission here. A ticketed guest is allowed to use the cloakroom. The guest could keep their coat on and never go inside.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Lena is a guest with a ticket. Do we know that she used the cloakroom?\\" options={[\'Yes, the ticket establishes that she used it.\', \'No, we know she is allowed to use it.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You turned permission into a completed action. Lena meets the condition for permission, but we have no fact reporting her use of the cloakroom.\', \'The rule gives Lena permission because she is a guest with a ticket. Whether she used the cloakroom remains open.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>Now compare an instruction. “If your coat is wet, hang it on the rack” tells you what to do with a wet coat. It does not report that someone followed the instruction.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"The notice says: If a tray is empty, return it to the counter. This tray is empty. What does the instruction establish?\\" options={[\'The tray has been returned.\', \'The instruction calls for returning the tray.\', \'The tray cannot be returned.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You turned an instruction into a completed action. The notice has not reported that anyone returned this tray.\', \'The empty tray meets the condition in the instruction, so the notice calls for returning it. Whether someone returned it is a separate question.\', \'The instruction asks for a return. It does not say a return is impossible.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>Allowed to use isn\'t used. Told to return isn\'t returned. Your conclusion should keep the meaning the sentence actually gave you.</p>\\r\\n    </section>\\r\\n  </div>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function ConditionalReferenceSequence() { return conditionalReferenceContent(); }\\r\\n\\r\\n// A long stage can contain several reading pages without changing the source order.\\r\\nexport function conditionalReferencePages(): LessonPage[] {\\r\\n"}'}]

Find the whole idea: a current membership.</p></div><div><blockquote>A current membership is required to borrow a studio camera.</blockquote><p>The same required idea now comes first. Moving it in the sentence hasn\'t changed what borrowing requires.</p></div></div>\\r\\n        <Arrow left=\\"Borrows studio camera\\" right=\\"Has current membership\\"/>\\r\\n        <ThinkPause prompt=\\"Mina has a current membership. Does this rule tell us she borrowed a camera?\\">\\r\\n          <p>No. Membership is something borrowing requires. Mina could have the membership and never borrow a camera. The rule tells us what we need if she borrows; having what she needs doesn\'t tell us she did.</p>\\r\\n        </ThinkPause>\\r\\n        <p>Notice the meaning shared by <strong>requires, necessitates, depends on,</strong> and <strong>relies on</strong> when they express a strict requirement. If borrowing depends on having a current membership, borrowing still requires membership. “Depends partly on” may describe an influence instead, so read the whole claim before treating it as a conditional.</p>\\r\\n        <p>You may also hear the requirement as “In order to borrow a camera, you must have a current membership.” The goal is borrowing; the required condition is membership. Only and only if can set the same restriction. We\'ll work through their wording next.</p>\\r\\n        <Check prompt=\\"Using the recording booth depends on having a reservation. What belongs on the right?\\" options={[\'Uses recording booth\', \'Has a reservation\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'Using the booth is what needs the reservation. Putting use on the right would make a reservation enough to establish that someone used the booth, which the sentence never says.\', \'A reservation is required for using the booth, so it belongs on the right. Having a reservation still leaves open whether the person uses it.\']}/>\\r\\n        <p>You won\'t always see a familiar word. Find what the sentence says is required <strong>for the other condition</strong>. Then check that your arrow keeps that requirement on the right.</p>\\r\\n      </>}\\r\\n    </Section>\\r\\n    {IndicatorSections({ id })}\\r\\n    <Section title={first ? \'Find the target, then place it\' : \'Find the requirement, then place it\'}>\\r\\n      <p>{first\\r\\n        ? \\"Add what to the indicator when that gives you a sensible question. If what? All what? The only what? Your answer should be the whole idea the expression refers to. Then check whether that idea really is enough to establish the other condition.\\"\\r\\n        : \\"Ask what the indicator refers to. Only what? Only if what? What is required? The target can come before or after the expression, so check its meaning in the complete sentence.\\"}</p>\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={4} label=\\"Necessary means required\\" title=\\"The other condition has to be there\\">\\r\\n      <blockquote>{raffleRule}</blockquote><p>The <strong>then-part</strong> is the <strong>necessary condition</strong>. Necessary means required. Under this rule, if you win, getting a bicycle has to follow.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-role-exhibit cr-required\\"><span>Necessary</span><strong>Get a bicycle</strong><p>Required whenever you win the raffle</p></div>\\r\\n      <p>Ask “required for what?” Here, a required result of winning under this rule. It is not a requirement you must satisfy before entering. The word necessary describes the relationship, not when the events occur.</p>\\r\\n      <p>We\'re looking at the same rule from its other side. Winning is enough to establish getting a bicycle. Getting a bicycle is the result the rule requires whenever you win.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Under our rule, what has to follow if you win?\\" options={[\'You get a bicycle.\', \'You ride the bicycle home.\']} correct={0} feedback={[\'Getting a bicycle is the stated result. Winning without getting one would violate the rule.\', \'Riding is not part of this rule. The sentence establishes that you get a bicycle, not what you do with it.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>Necessary does not mean “the next event.” It means required by this relationship. A conditional need not tell you which event caused another, or when either happened.</p>\\r\\n      <p>As with sufficient language, the wording can vary while the relationship stays the same.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={5} label=\\"The necessary family\\" title=\\"Listen for what the sentence needs\\">\\r\\n      <p>Return to our locker rule. Borrowing a locker requires a key. The next expressions all identify that requirement in their complete sentences.</p>\\r\\n      <WordFamily entries={necessaryFamily} role=\\"necessary\\"/>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-contrast\\"><div><h3>If</h3><p>“You borrow a locker <strong>if</strong> you have a key.”</p><p>Having a key is enough for borrowing under this sentence.</p></div><div><h3>Only if</h3><p>“You borrow a locker <strong>only if</strong> you have a key.”</p><p>Having a key is required. This sentence has not made it enough.</p></div></div>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"A guest enters the lounge only if the guest has a current pass. What does entering establish?\\" options={[\'The guest has a current pass.\', \'Every guest with a pass enters.\']} correct={0} feedback={[\'Only if identifies the current pass as required for entry. An entering guest therefore meets that requirement.\', \'You made the requirement enough. A guest could have a current pass and remain outside without violating the sentence.\']}/>\\r\\n"}'}]

Verified: new course components do not write completion, query parameters survive navigation, and denied step IDs do not render their content. Both findings were sent directly to Astra.

## assistant

The two substantive routing fixes are verified:

- Opening “Begin lesson” now enters the new Lessons index.
- Explicit source-unit mappings prevent a sufficient/necessary-only assignment from opening orientation’s contrapositive material.

One minor fix remains with Astra: the new root-entry link retains `assignment` but drops other existing query parameters. Navigation inside the course preserves them.

No implicit completion writes found. Restricted and practice-only assignments remain filtered. Final browser focus verification belongs to the parent’s test pass.

Their stateful exercises are\\r\\n// mounted by React; the former reader-page renderer is never invoked here.\\r\\nfunction sections(children: ReactNode): ContentSection[] {\\r\\n  return Children.toArray(children).flatMap(child => {\\r\\n    if (!isValidElement<ContentSection[\'props\']>(child)) return [];\\r\\n    return child.type === Fragment ? sections(child.props.children) : [child];\\r\\n  });\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction reference(number: number): ContentSection {\\r\\n  const section = sections(conditionalReferenceContent().props.children).find(item => item.props.number === number);\\r\\n  if (!section) throw new Error(`Missing approved conditional reference section ${number}`);\\r\\n  return section;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction groupSections(group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\') {\\r\\n  return sections(GroupLessons({ id: group }).props.children);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction groupSection(group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\', title: string) {\\r\\n  const section = groupSections(group).find(item => item.props.title === title);\\r\\n  if (!section) throw new Error(`Missing approved conditional section: ${title}`);\\r\\n  return cloneElement(section, { id: `course-${group}-${title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, \'-\')}` });\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction NoteSection({ title, children }: { title: string; children: ReactNode }) {\\r\\n  return <section className=\\"co-section\\"><div className=\\"co-section-heading\\"><h2>{title}</h2></div>{children}</section>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction ReferenceBody({ number, omitTransition = false }: { number: number; omitTransition?: boolean }) {\\r\\n  const source = reference(number);\\r\\n  const children = Children.toArray(source.props.children);\\r\\n  // These source sections end in navigation prose for the former ordering.\\r\\n  // The course shell now owns transitions; the teaching stays in its source.\\r\\n  return <section className={`co-section cr-course-section ${source.props.dark ? \'cr-dark\' : \'\'}`} data-reference-source={number}>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-section-heading\\"><h2>{source.props.title}</h2></div>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"cr-step-body\\">{omitTransition ? children.slice(0, -1) : children}</div>\\r\\n  </section>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction FamilySupplement({ group }: { group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\' }) {\\r\\n  const source = reference(group === \'group-1\' ? 3 : 5);\\r\\n  const family = sections(source.props.children).find(child => child.type === WordFamily);\\r\\n  if (!family) throw new Error(`Missing approved ${group} supplementary family`);\\r\\n  return <details className=\\"co-practical-note\\"><summary>More expressions for the same relationship</summary>\\r\\n    <p>Use the stated rule: anyone who borrows a locker has a key. These sentences preserve that connection. They do not say every person with a key borrows a locker.</p>\\r\\n    {family}\\r\\n  </details>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction IndicatorNote({ group }: { group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\' }) {\\r\\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(0);\\r\\n  const id = useId();\\r\\n  const content = groupSections(group);\\r\\n  const expressions = content.slice(2, 9);\\r\\n  // Two introductions and the seven complete expression explanations belong\\r\\n  // together in one concept note, not nine separate navigation destinations.\\r\\n  return <>{content.slice(0, 2)}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-word-tabs\\" role=\\"group\\" aria-label=\\"Choose an expression\\">{expressions.map((section, index) => <button type=\\"button\\" key={section.props.title} aria-pressed={selected === index} aria-controls={`${id}-${index}`} onClick={() => setSelected(index)}>{section.props.title?.split(\':\')[0]}</button>)}</div>\\r\\n    {expressions.map((section, index) => <div key={section.props.title} id={`${id}-${index}`} hidden={selected !== index}>{section}</div>)}\\r\\n    <FamilySupplement group={group}/>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Recall the expressions\\"><p>Explain the relationship before turning each card. Compare the complete ideas and the direction with your answer.</p><StudyDeck group={group}/></NoteSection>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction FoundationPractice() {\\r\\n  const definitionQuestions = [1, 2, 4].flatMap(number => sections(reference(number).props.children).filter(child => child.type === ReferenceQuestion).map((child, index) => cloneElement(child, { key: `${number}-${index}` })));\\r\\n  const fresh = sections(Fundamentals().props.children).find(section => section.props.title === \'Enough does not mean the only way\');\\r\\n  if (!fresh) throw new Error(\'Missing approved fresh sufficient-condition check\');\\r\\n  const freshContent = Children.toArray(fresh.props.children);\\r\\n  const freshCheck = freshContent[freshContent.length - 1];\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Separate the rule from the fact\\"><blockquote>If you win the raffle, you get a bicycle.</blockquote><p>Use the rule to decide what each fact establishes. A wrong answer is a reason to inspect the connection and try again.</p>{definitionQuestions}</NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Try a fresh case\\">{freshCheck}</NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Test the limit with a possible case\\"><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Someone claims that getting a bicycle proves you won the raffle. Which possible case fits our rule but disproves that claim?\\" options={[\'You win and get a bicycle.\', \'You do not win, but get a bicycle as a gift.\', \'You win and never get a bicycle.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'This fits both the rule and the claim. It does not show why the claim adds something.\', \'The rule promises a bicycle to a winner. It does not exclude a bicycle received as a gift without winning, so this case fits the rule and disproves the claim.\', \'Winning without getting a bicycle breaks the original rule. We need a case that keeps the rule true.\']}/></NoteSection>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction GroupPractice({ group }: { group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\' }) {\\r\\n  const meaningCheck = groupSection(group, \'Check the meaning, not just the word\');\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    {groupSection(group, group === \'group-1\' ? \'Find the target, then place it\' : \'Find the requirement, then place it\')}\\r\\n    {groupSection(group, \'From sentence to diagram\')}\\r\\n    {group === \'group-1\' && groupSection(group, \'Read the only as a complete expression\')}\\r\\n    {cloneElement(meaningCheck, {}, Children.toArray(meaningCheck.props.children).slice(0, -1))}\\r\\n    <details className=\\"co-practical-note\\"><summary>More sentences to recall and explain</summary>{groupSection(group, \'Say the rule without the clues\')}</details>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction PermissionBoundary() {\\r\\n  const boundary = sections(conditionalReferenceContent().props.children).find(section => section.props[\'data-reference-boundary\'] !== undefined);\\r\\n  if (!boundary) throw new Error(\'Missing approved permission and instruction boundary\');\\r\\n  return <NoteSection title=\\"Keep permission and instructions distinct\\"><p>A conditional can give permission or an instruction. Preserve that strength instead of turning it into a report of what someone did.</p>{Children.toArray(boundary.props.children).slice(3)}</NoteSection>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction ContrapositivePractice() {\\r\\n  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(0);\\r\\n  const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean[]>(() => referencePracticeItems.map(() => false));\\r\\n  return <NoteSection title=\\"Build an original and its contrapositive\\">\\r\\n    <p>For each sentence, identify the indicator and both complete conditions. Choose the original diagram, then its contrapositive. Read both back before checking. If an answer needs revision, inspect the direction, qualifications and negation, then retry.</p>\\r\\n    <p className=\\"co-kicker\\" role=\\"status\\">Sentence {current + 1} of {referencePracticeItems.length}</p>\\r\\n    {referencePracticeItems.map((item, index) => <div key={item.sentence} hidden={current !== index} data-course-practice-item={index + 1}><IntegratedItem item={item} number={index + 1} onChecked={value => setChecked(previous => previous.map((old, itemIndex) => itemIndex === index ? value : old))}/></div>)}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-choices\\"><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === 0} onClick={() => setCurrent(current - 1)}>Previous sentence</button><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === referencePracticeItems.length - 1 || !checked[current]} onClick={() => setCurrent(current + 1)}>Next sentence</button></div>\\r\\n    <p>Moving between sentences keeps your choices and feedback.</p>\\r\\n  </NoteSection>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction Content({ id }: { id: string }) {\\r\\n  switch (id) {\\r\\n    case \'meaning\': return <ReferenceBody number={1} omitTransition/>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient\': return <ReferenceBody number={2} omitTransition/>;\\r\\n    case \'necessary\': return <><ReferenceBody number={4} omitTransition/><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"You get a bicycle. Does that establish that you won the raffle?\\" options={[\'Yes. Getting a bicycle proves winning.\', \'No. You could get a bicycle without winning.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You made the required result enough to establish winning. The rule does not say winning is the only way to get a bicycle.\', \'You could buy a bicycle or receive one as a gift. Neither possibility breaks the rule, which only tells us what must follow if you win.\']}/></>;\\r\\n    case \'must-arrow\': return <><ReferenceBody number={8}/><NoteSection title=\\"Recall enough and required\\"><p>Use these new examples to check the roles and their direction.</p><StudyDeck group=\\"foundation\\"/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient-words\': return <IndicatorNote group=\\"group-1\\"/>;\\r\\n    case \'necessary-words\': return <><IndicatorNote group=\\"group-2\\"/><PermissionBoundary/></>;\\r\\n    case \'whole-meaning\': return <><ReferenceBody number={11} omitTransition/>{groupSection(\'group-1\', \'Keep the whole condition\')}{groupSection(\'group-2\', \'Keep the whole condition\')}{groupSection(\'group-2\', \'Compare only with the only\')}<ReferenceBody number={12} omitTransition/></>;\\r\\n    case \'missing-requirement\': return <><ReferenceBody number={6}/><ReferenceBody number={7} omitTransition/></>;\\r\\n    case \'contrapositive\': return <><ReferenceBody number={9}/><details className=\\"co-practical-note\\"><summary>Practical questions about diagramming</summary><ReferenceBody number={10} omitTransition/></details><NoteSection title=\\"Two possible rooms, one limit\\"><NegativeCaseLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'foundation-practice\': return <FoundationPractice/>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient-practice\': return <><GroupPractice group=\\"group-1\\"/><NoteSection title=\\"Build a case that proves the limit\\"><CounterexampleLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'mixed-practice\': return <><GroupPractice group=\\"group-2\\"/><NoteSection title=\\"Keep the rule while the wording changes\\"><RuleComparisonLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'contrapositive-practice\': return <ContrapositivePractice/>;\\r\\n    default: throw new Error(`Unknown opening course content: ${id}`);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Article body only. Course routes own titles, navigation and completion. */\\r\\nexport function OpeningCourseContent({ id }: { id: string }) {\\r\\n  return <div className=\\"co-opening cr-sequence opening-course-content\\"><Content key={id} id={id}/></div>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n---\\r\\ntype: synthesis\\r\\nsubject: LSAT teaching voice standard\\r\\ncreated: 2026-10-02\\r\\nupdated: 2026-10-03\\r\\naliases: [LSAT voice reference, Conditional transcription writing standard]\\r\\ntags: [lsat-u, voice, pedagogy, writing]\\r\\nsources:\\r\\n  - ../wiki/sources/conditional-reasoning-voice.md\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT teaching: make the reasoning sound like someone thinking\\r\\n\\r\\n**This is Joshua\'s selected reference for writing LSAT teaching material.** Use it for bootcamp lessons, lecture notes, explanations, guided examples, drills, flashcards, quizzes, reference pages, and instructional feedback. It develops the teaching-content register in [the canonical teaching voice](../wiki/teaching-voice.md). That document still governs correspondence and marketing in their own registers.\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua selected the supplied **Conditional Reasoning** transcription on 2026-10-02 because of its writing, tone, word choice, cadence, point of view, progression, and depth. The goal is to reproduce those qualities closely through original wording and examples. The central quality is patient, conversational reasoning that the reader can follow and eventually perform.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe source is a calibration example. This guide separates **observed features** from **instructions for our material**. A source habit is not automatically a rule, a research finding, or permission to import a topic. Matching the voice does not require repeating the same metaphors, anecdotes, exercise sentences, or personal claims.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Find the part you need\\r\\n\\r\\n- [The evidence and coverage](#the-evidence-and-coverage)\\r\\n- [The voice in one original passage](#the-voice-in-one-original-passage)\\r\\n- [How the teacher relates to the reader](#how-the-teacher-relates-to-the-reader)\\r\\n- [Sentence length and spoken cadence](#sentence-length-and-spoken-cadence)\\r\\n- [Word choice and useful verbal habits](#word-choice-and-useful-verbal-habits)\\r\\n- [Questions that make the reader think](#questions-that-make-the-reader-think)\\r\\n- [Transitions, repetition, metaphor, and emphasis](#transitions-explain-why-the-next-move-follows)\\r\\n- [The complete source progression and depth](#the-complete-source-progression-and-depth)\\r\\n- [What to carry into the Conditional Bootcamp](#what-to-carry-into-the-conditional-bootcamp)\\r\\n- [Accuracy and method boundaries](#accuracy-and-method-boundaries)\\r\\n- [Calibration examples and review](#calibration-examples-for-different-lsat-surfaces)\\r\\n- [A reusable writing brief](#a-reusable-writing-brief)\\r\\n\\r\\n## The evidence and coverage\\r\\n\\r\\nThe [source summary](../wiki/sources/conditional-reasoning-voice.md) identifies the [preserved HTML](../raw/sources/conditional-reasoning-voice-standard/conditional_reasoning_transcription.html), [provenance](../raw/sources/conditional-reasoning-voice-standard/PROVENANCE.md), and SHA-256. Every supplied section, FAQ entry, table, worked diagram, and drill item was read. HTML line references below refer to that unchanged archived file.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe document has six main sections and six subordinate headings. It ends with six basic drill items and an answer-key reference. One line is explicitly marked partially obscured. The answer key is not supplied. This analysis covers the entire attachment; it cannot reconstruct the missing line or establish the contents of the larger chapter.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe HTML says its formatting was adjusted. We can examine what a pause, table, side note, or separated example does for learning. We cannot claim its font, spacing, color, or CSS exactly reproduces the original publication. No author is identified in the file. The exercise wording attributed to Shakespeare is separate from the narrator\'s teaching voice.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The voice in one original passage\\r\\n\\r\\nThe following is a new calibration passage. Its example was created for this guide; it is not a source quotation or an approved bootcamp page.\\r\\n\\r\\n> A conditional tells us that if one thing is true, something else has to be true too.\\r\\n>\\r\\n> Suppose a shop has this rule: **Every parcel with a blue sticker has been inspected.**\\r\\n>\\r\\n> You pick up a parcel with a blue sticker. What do you know about it?\\r\\n>\\r\\n> It has been inspected. The rule covers every parcel with that sticker, including the one in your hand. A blue-sticker parcel that hadn\'t been inspected would break the rule.\\r\\n>\\r\\n> Now turn the parcel over. It has an inspection stamp, but you can\'t see a blue sticker. Does it have to have one?\\r\\n>\\r\\n> We don\'t know. The rule tells us something about parcels with blue stickers. It doesn\'t tell us that every inspected parcel gets a sticker.\\r\\n>\\r\\n> That\'s the distinction we need: **what the sentence makes certain, and what it leaves open.**\\r\\n\\r\\nNotice the opening definition before the example, the small prediction, the explanation connecting the rule to the case, and the change in what the reader is given. The last sentence names a distinction the reader has just seen. The passage has a conversational rhythm because it follows a person\'s thoughts. Casual vocabulary alone would not accomplish that.\\r\\n\\r\\nIn an interactive lesson, pause after the first question and again after the inspection-stamp question. Reveal each explanation after the learner has had an opportunity to answer. The printed passage shows the whole progression for calibration.\\r\\n\\r\\n## How the teacher relates to the reader\\r\\n\\r\\n### The reader is beside the teacher\\r\\n\\r\\nThe narrator talks directly to someone doing the work. “Let\'s,” “you,” and “we” keep the reader involved. The writing seldom steps back to describe what students generally do. It asks this reader to notice, try, decide, or check something now.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe reader is treated as capable of understanding ordinary meaning. The teacher supplies support when a technical step is new. In the opening, the source first gives the literal relationship, then asks the reader to take its certainty seriously. Later, it encourages a guess before revealing the contrapositive. These are expectations of participation, not claims that everything should feel easy.\\r\\n\\r\\n**For our writing:** speak to the reader without making their intelligence the subject. Do not copy a line such as “Because you\'re a thinking human.” Give them a manageable question and the information to answer it. If they miss it, explain the precise move that went wrong.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Confidence lives in the reasoning\\r\\n\\r\\nThe source is decisive about a valid consequence. It also says “We don\'t know” when the information cannot settle a question. These two kinds of confidence belong together. Clear teaching can be certain about the limits of what is known.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe teacher does not apologize for asking the reader to think. The explanation makes the request reasonable. In the FAQ, the narrator acknowledges early mistakes and explains the value of practicing anyway. The tone combines patience with a specific demand: attempt the question, write the diagram, inspect the error.\\r\\n\\r\\n**For our writing:** state the consequence plainly and show why. Preserve legitimate uncertainty. Avoid changing a logical “could” into “must” to make the prose sound stronger. Avoid guarantees about learning outcomes, timing, or score changes unless we have evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Warmth points at the work\\r\\n\\r\\nEncouragement is usually tied to an action. The reader can look back at the lesson, make a provisional attempt, learn from a wrong translation, or build confidence by checking work. The warmth comes from useful help and a teacher who expects progress.\\r\\n\\r\\nUseful form:\\r\\n\\r\\n> If the direction felt unclear, read the statement back in ordinary English. What does it say you need? Keep that complete idea in your diagram.\\r\\n\\r\\nWeak form:\\r\\n\\r\\n> You\'ve got this! Conditionals are easy once you know the trick!\\r\\n\\r\\nThe weak version offers reassurance without a way forward and minimizes the actual difficulty.\\r\\n\\r\\n### “I,” “we,” and “you” have different jobs\\r\\n\\r\\n| Pronoun | What it does in the source | Use in our material |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| **You** | Gives the reader an action or asks for a decision. | “Try the sentence in the other direction. Does it still say the same thing?” |\\r\\n| **We / let\'s** | Makes the explanation a shared investigation. | “Let\'s keep the rule and change the fact.” |\\r\\n| **I**, thinking aloud | Shows the teacher making a decision: noticing an indicator, identifying its target, placing a label. | “I see ‘requires.’ What does it say is required?” |\\r\\n| **I**, hypothetical | Places the speaker inside a condition. | “If I\'m taking this course, what does the sentence say I need?” |\\r\\n| **I**, personal judgment | Gives a recommendation or reports experience. | Use only a genuine Joshua judgment or verified experience. Do not borrow the source narrator\'s student history. |\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep these roles stable. Do not rotate pronouns for cosmetic variety. In a platform instruction, “you” may be enough. In a teacher-authored walkthrough, “I” can make a decision visible. Marketing remains governed by its separate platform voice.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Sentence length and spoken cadence\\r\\n\\r\\n"}'}]

Production/authenticated persistence and student learning outcomes remain unverified by this review.\n+\n+## 2026-10-04 concept-page pacing audit after course reconstruction\n+\n+Read-only application review. Compared the current nine-note/four-lab composition with actual Intro to LR source, using `references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md` as the writing authority. Parent separately inspected authenticated live IntroLR; this reviewer did not repeat that browser inspection. Findings below concern source composition and instructional judgment, not measured learning outcomes or timings. No application edits were made.\n+\n+### What the reference actually divides\n+\n+`src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/content/introToLrPath.ts` organizes eight concept notes, three standalone labs and two practice sets. `modules/lessons/notes/IntroLessonPage.tsx:451–539` keeps the Premises definition, contrast, indicators and short checked application together. Conclusions (`:546–651`) similarly joins the claim, language and checked identification. Five Types (`:654–756`) teaches examples, then a switchboard, followed by its separate lab in the path. These are conceptual articles, not one example per route. The conditional nine-note/four-lab structure now follows that useful pattern. Keep the dedicated meaning, sufficient and necessary destinations; none needs padding merely to equal the length of an indicator lesson.\n+\n+The reference is not uniformly better: its Beyond Premises note has no rendered role-labeling exercise, despite unused imports; its structure note's ClaimBucketInspector reveals definitions rather than assessing classifications. Do not copy those gaps or count them as independent practice.\n+\n+### Ranked findings and proposed corrections\n+\n+1. **Narrow the must-arrow lesson to its stated job.** Evidence: `OpeningCourseContent.tsx:121` imports all of reference stage 8 (`ConditionalReferenceSequence.tsx:259–285`). Besides arrow roles and a moved if-clause, that section already teaches both indicator families, only versus only if, and required/requires target placement. Those topics recur in the following indicator notes and whole-meaning note. Keep the arrow meaning, one raffle diagram, moved if-clause, incremental writer and its check here. Move the full only/only-if comparison to Necessary-condition words and target-before/after contrast to Keep the whole meaning. This is a pacing recommendation grounded in visible repeated content; it is not a claim that the earlier material is logically wrong.\n+\n+2. **Make the first lab transfer the ideas instead of immediately replaying the same questions.** `FoundationPractice` (`OpeningCourseContent.tsx:74`) extracts the four exact ReferenceQuestion elements from stages 1, 2 and 4. Learners have just answered these on the preceding three notes. Two further tasks add value: a fresh collected-delivery example and a counterexample choice. Keep one raffle retrieval question as a bridge; replace the other three repeated prompts with fresh, short cases testing rule versus fact, sufficient versus necessary, and what stays open. Keep notation out. The voice standard says to repeat an anchor when the repetition changes the learner's view, rather than merely repeat wording.\n+\n+3. **Make the mixed lab genuinely mix diagram production.** `OpeningCourseContent.tsx:129` runs `GroupPractice` only for group 2, so its target finder and diagram builder use the seven necessary-family examples. `CounterexampleLab.tsx:28–50` then supplies four envelope equivalence judgments, including if and the only. That is meaningful comparison, but the bulk of the run still announces the family before every translation. Keep the envelope contrast; add a short alternating set of sufficient- and necessary-family sentences with the group label withheld, requiring target identification and arrow construction. Do not add another destination. This better tests the stated mixed-family purpose; no universal benefit is asserted.\n+\n+4. **Give Keep the whole meaning one visible progression.** `OpeningCourseContent.tsx:124` concatenates five substantial blocks: target-position lesson, two separately titled Keep the whole condition sections, only/the only comparison, and Personalized If/Then plus What Test. The two qualification cases are useful contrasts, not identical material, but the repeated heading restarts the explanation. Combine them as one paired qualification check (late applicant/current pass), then present target position, only/the only, and the imagined-case test as successive checks on one translation process. A short orienting sentence should explain what each check catches. Prefer this consolidation before splitting another page.\n+\n+5. **Signal the intended expression-selector path before the cards.** `IndicatorNote` (`OpeningCourseContent.tsx:59–71`) defaults to expression one, keeps six panels hidden, then presents the full 10- or 11-card family deck. A reader can naturally scroll to cards without opening the other six named examples. This is an affordance issue, not grounds for a mastery lock. Add concise guidance to work through each expression, and a local next-expression affordance or viewed-position cue. Offer the deck as retrieval after those examples. Keep manual selection and revisit state.\n+\n+6. **Use one fresh bridge case in the early definition notes, not more explanation.** The first three notes correctly use the raffle to distinguish rule/fact, enough and required, and already include checks. The fresh case currently arrives in the lab. Optionally add one compact comparison to Necessary (required result versus an earlier entry requirement) before its final check, using the existing temporal clarification as the model. This is a lower-priority design preference; the current definition is accurate and the lab already supplies transfer.\n+\n+### Preserve during revision\n+\n+Keep nine genuine concept destinations and four practice transitions; no return to the 70-page reader. Retain the approved raffle anchor, first-three-note notation boundary, complete expression inventories and modality caveats, all 25 cards, both Demon-derived exercises, four cases, sign patterns and six paired final exercises. Preserve attempt-before-feedback, retry and retained answers. Do not interpret reviewed reading or card flips as assessed mastery. No route, assignment, backend or completion-policy change is proposed by this pacing audit.\n+\n+Recommended order: resolve findings 1–3 first, then consolidate whole-meaning and improve expression navigation. Finding 6 is optional. The evidence supports improving task boundaries and repetition, not a particular word count or a guarantee of retention.\n*** End Patch"));
