Only if appears in the middle, but it still identifies the necessary condition.\']}/>\\r\\n  </NoteSection>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction IndicatorNote({ group }: { group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\' }) {\\r\\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(0);\\r\\n  const [opened, setOpened] = useState<number[]>([0]);\\r\\n  const [focusPanel, setFocusPanel] = useState(false);\\r\\n  const panels = useRef<(HTMLDivElement | null)[]>([]);\\r\\n  const id = useId();\\r\\n  const content = groupSections(group);\\r\\n  const expressions = content.slice(2, 9);\\r\\n  const names = expressions.map(section => section.props.title?.split(\':\')[0]);\\r\\n  useEffect(() => {\\r\\n    if (!focusPanel) return;\\r\\n    panels.current[selected]?.focus();\\r\\n    setFocusPanel(false);\\r\\n  }, [focusPanel, selected]);\\r\\n  const choose = (index: number, moveFocus = false) => {\\r\\n    setSelected(index);\\r\\n    setOpened(previous => previous.includes(index) ? previous : [...previous, index]);\\r\\n    setFocusPanel(moveFocus);\\r\\n  };\\r\\n  const last = selected === expressions.length - 1;\\r\\n  // Two introductions and the seven complete expression explanations belong\\r\\n  // together in one concept note, not nine separate navigation destinations.\\r\\n  return <>{content.slice(0, 2)}\\r\\n    <p className=\\"co-word-guide\\">Work through all seven expressions. Each one does the same job in a different sentence, and each has its own trap to check. Use Next expression to go in order, or choose any expression to read it again.</p>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-word-tabs\\" role=\\"group\\" aria-label=\\"Choose an expression\\">{expressions.map((section, index) => <button type=\\"button\\" key={section.props.title} aria-pressed={selected === index} aria-controls={`${id}-${index}`} onClick={() => choose(index)}>{names[index]}{opened.includes(index) && <><span aria-hidden=\\"true\\"> ✓</span><span className=\\"co-sr-only\\">, opened</span></>}</button>)}</div>\\r\\n    <p className=\\"co-kicker\\" role=\\"status\\">Expression {selected + 1} of {expressions.length} · {opened.length} of {expressions.length} opened</p>\\r\\n    {expressions.map((section, index) => <div key={section.props.title} id={`${id}-${index}`} hidden={selected !== index} tabIndex={-1} ref={element => { panels.current[index] = element; }}>{section}</div>)}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-choices\\">{last\\r\\n      ? <p>That was the last of the seven expressions. Choose any of them to read it again, or recall them with the cards below.</p>\\r\\n      : <button type=\\"button\\" className=\\"co-primary\\" onClick={() => choose(selected + 1, true)}>Next expression: {names[selected + 1]}</button>}</div>\\r\\n    {group === \'group-2\' && <OnlyAndOnlyIf/>}\\r\\n    <FamilySupplement group={group}/>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Recall the expressions\\"><p>Once you\'ve read the seven examples, use these cards to recall them. Explain the relationship before turning each card, then compare the complete ideas and the direction with your answer.</p><StudyDeck group={group}/></NoteSection>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n// The raffle note sits before the families: arrow meaning, sides, one diagram and a moved if-clause.\\r\\nfunction MustArrowNote() {\\r\\n  return <section className=\\"co-section cr-course-section\\" data-reference-source={8}>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-section-heading\\"><h2>Give the relationship a shorter form</h2></div>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"cr-step-body\\">\\r\\n      <p>Put the sufficient condition on the <strong>left</strong>, the necessary condition on the <strong>right</strong>, and a <strong>must arrow</strong> between them.</p>\\r\\n      <RuleDiagram left=\\"Sufficient: enough\\" right=\\"Necessary: required\\"/>\\r\\n      <p>Read the arrow as <strong>must</strong>: if the left condition is true, the right condition must be true too. It does not mean the left caused the right, or that the right happens later.</p>\\r\\n      <p>The diagram holds the <strong>complete conditions</strong>, not the indicator word. An indicator helps you find a condition\'s job. Once you\'ve found that job, place the whole condition on its side of the arrow.</p>\\r\\n      <h3>Build the raffle diagram one step at a time</h3>\\r\\n      <p>First find the indicator, then draw the arrow, place the complete idea it refers to, and fill the other side.</p>\\r\\n      <IncrementalWriter/>\\r\\n      <h3>The sentence can move. The roles stay the same.</h3>\\r\\n      <p>Compare these two versions of our raffle rule. The indicator is bold; the complete idea it refers to is in brackets.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-language-pair\\"><p><strong>If</strong> [you win the raffle], you get a bicycle.</p><p>You get a bicycle <strong>if</strong> [you win the raffle].</p><span>If identifies the sufficient condition in both sentences.</span></div>\\r\\n      <p>In the second sentence, if appears in the middle. Its condition comes last, but winning is still enough to establish getting a bicycle. Don\'t let the first phrase in English choose the first side of your diagram.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"You get a bicycle if you win the raffle. Which diagram preserves this sentence?\\" options={[\'Get bicycle → Win\', \'Win → Get bicycle\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You let sentence order choose the arrow. The if-clause still makes winning enough for getting a bicycle.\', \'The sufficient condition is still winning. Where it appears in the sentence does not change what it establishes.\']}/>\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  </section>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n// One translation process, checked four ways, instead of five restarted lessons.\\r\\nfunction WholeMeaningNote() {\\r\\n  const onlyComparison = groupSection(\'group-2\', \'Compare only with the only\');\\r\\n  const insideCheck = Children.toArray(reference(12).props.children);\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Check a translation four ways\\">\\r\\n      <p>A diagram can point the right way and still say the wrong thing. Each check below catches a different slip in the same translation process.</p>\\r\\n      <ol>\\r\\n        <li><strong>Target:</strong> did you find the whole idea the indicator refers to, wherever it sits?</li>\\r\\n        <li><strong>Qualification:</strong> did your short label keep every restriction?</li>\\r\\n        <li><strong>Direction:</strong> did a similar-looking expression trick you into the wrong side?</li>\\r\\n        <li><strong>Imagined case:</strong> does your arrow promise something the sentence leaves open?</li>\\r\\n      </ol>\\r\\n    </NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Check 1: find the whole target, wherever it sits\\">\\r\\n      <p>An indicator\'s <strong>target</strong> is the complete word or phrase it refers to. In “All guests wearing blue badges receive vouchers,” all refers to guests wearing blue badges, not guests alone.</p>\\r\\n      <p>The target often comes after its indicator. But often isn\'t always. Try these sentences in order.</p>\\r\\n      {targetExamples.map(item => <TargetReader item={item} key={item.label}/>)}\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-language-pair\\"><p>[Having a key] is <strong>required</strong> for borrowing a locker.</p><p>Borrowing a locker <strong>requires</strong> [having a key].</p><span>Having a key is the requirement in both sentences.</span></div>\\r\\n      <p>The target comes before required in the first sentence and after requires in the second. Having a key still goes right. Neither the closest noun nor the next word is a reliable target rule. Ask which complete idea the sentence calls required, then give that idea its role.</p>\\r\\n    </NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Check 2: keep every qualification\\">\\r\\n      <p>Once you have the target, shorten it without losing what limits it. These two sentences test the same habit from opposite sides of the arrow.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"co-word-comparison\\">\\r\\n        <div><blockquote>Any applicant who submits late pays a fee.</blockquote><p>Applicant alone isn\'t the condition. The sentence is about an applicant who submits late. Drop that restriction and your diagram makes a claim about on-time applicants too.</p></div>\\r\\n        <div><blockquote>Entry requires a current pass.</blockquote><p>A current pass is required. Has a pass drops current and would include an expired pass. A shorter label should save writing, not change the requirement.</p></div>\\r\\n      </div>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Any applicant who submits late pays a fee. What goes left?\\" options={[\'Applicant\', \'Applicant submits late\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You dropped the late-submission restriction. Applicant alone would cover every applicant, including someone who submits on time. The sufficient idea is applicant submits late.\', \'This keeps the complete sufficient idea. The rule covers applicants who submit late, so keep that restriction with the applicant.\']}/>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Entry requires a current pass. What goes right?\\" options={[\'Has current pass\', \'Has any pass\']} correct={0} feedback={[\'This keeps the full requirement. Entry needs a current pass; an expired pass does not meet that requirement.\', \'You dropped current from the requirement. Has any pass would include an expired pass, which is not what the sentence requires.\']}/>\\r\\n    </NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Check 3: only and the only point to different targets\\">{onlyComparison.props.children}</NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Check 4: try the sentence from the inside\\">{insideCheck.slice(0, -1)}</NoteSection>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nconst freshCases = [\\r\\n  { rule: \'If it rains on Saturday, the market moves into the town hall.\', questions: [\\r\\n    { prompt: \\"It\'s Friday. You\'ve read this rule and nothing else. Where will the market be on Saturday?\\", options: [\'In the town hall.\', \'Outdoors, as usual.\', \\"The rule alone doesn\'t settle it.\\"], correct: 2, feedback: [\'You treated the rule as a weather report. It tells you what follows if it rains. Nobody has told you that it will rain.\', \\"You assumed it won\'t rain. The rule hasn\'t told you that either, so the market\'s location is still open.\\", \\"The rule describes what would happen if it rains. It\'s a promise about a possible case, not a report that the case happened.\\"] },\\r\\n    { prompt: \\"Saturday arrives, and it\'s raining. Now where is the market?\\", options: [\'In the town hall.\', \'Still not settled.\'], correct: 0, feedback: [\'Now you have a fact, not just a rule. Rain on Saturday meets the condition, so the rule puts the market in the town hall.\', \\"The fact changes things. The rule covers a rainy Saturday, and that\'s what we have, so the market\'s location is settled.\\"] },\\r\\n  ] },\\r\\n  { rule: \'Every student going on the museum trip has a signed permission slip.\', questions: [\\r\\n    { prompt: \'Which description matches this rule?\', options: [\'Going on the trip is enough to know a student has a signed slip.\', \'Having a signed slip is enough to know a student is going on the trip.\', \'Each one is enough to know the other.\'], correct: 0, feedback: [\'Pick any student on the trip: the rule says they have a signed slip. Going is enough to establish the slip, and the slip is what every student on the trip is required to have.\', \\"You made the requirement enough. A student could have a signed slip and stay at school with a cold. That student doesn\'t break the rule.\\", \\"The rule gives only one direction. Going on the trip establishes a signed slip. A student with a slip who stays behind fits the rule, so the slip doesn\'t establish going.\\"] },\\r\\n  ] },\\r\\n  { rule: \'If the café runs out of bread, it closes early.\', questions: [\\r\\n    { prompt: \'Today the café did not run out of bread. Did it close early?\', options: [\'No. It stayed open until the usual time.\', \'Yes. It closed early.\', \'Not settled. It could stay open or close early for another reason.\'], correct: 2, feedback: [\'You treated running out of bread as the only reason to close early. The rule gives one reason. A café that closed early because of a power cut would still fit it.\', \\"Nothing here establishes an early closing. The rule tells us what happens when the bread runs out, and today it didn\'t.\\", \'Without the bread running out, the rule has nothing to tell us about today. The café could stay open, or close early for another reason. Both cases fit the rule.\'] },\\r\\n  ] },\\r\\n];\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction FoundationPractice() {\\r\\n  const anchor = sections(reference(1).props.children).find(child => child.type === ReferenceQuestion);\\r\\n  if (!anchor) throw new Error(\'Missing approved raffle retrieval question\');\\r\\n  const fresh = sections(Fundamentals().props.children).find(section => section.props.title === \'Enough does not mean the only way\');\\r\\n  if (!fresh) throw new Error(\'Missing approved fresh sufficient-condition check\');\\r\\n  const freshContent = Children.toArray(fresh.props.children);\\r\\n  const freshCheck = freshContent[freshContent.length - 1];\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Separate the rule from the fact\\"><blockquote>If you win the raffle, you get a bicycle.</blockquote><p>Start with the rule you know. Decide what the rule itself establishes before any fact arrives.</p>{anchor}</NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Carry the ideas to new rules\\">\\r\\n      <p>Now the situations change. Take each rule as given and decide what it establishes, what it requires and what it leaves open. A wrong answer is a reason to inspect the connection and try again.</p>\\r\\n      {freshCases.map(item => <div key={item.rule} className=\\"co-fresh-case\\"><blockquote>{item.rule}</blockquote>{item.questions.map(question => <ReferenceQuestion key={question.prompt} {...question}/>)}</div>)}\\r\\n    </NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Try a fresh case\\">{freshCheck}</NoteSection>\\r\\n    <NoteSection title=\\"Test the limit with a possible case\\"><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Someone claims that getting a bicycle proves you won the raffle. Which possible case fits our rule but disproves that claim?\\" options={[\'You win and get a bicycle.\', \'You do not win, but get a bicycle as a gift.\', \'You win and never get a bicycle.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'This fits both the rule and the claim. It does not show why the claim adds something.\', \'The rule promises a bicycle to a winner. It does not exclude a bicycle received as a gift without winning, so this case fits the rule and disproves the claim.\', \'Winning without getting a bicycle breaks the original rule. We need a case that keeps the rule true.\']}/></NoteSection>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction GroupPractice({ group }: { group: \'group-1\' | \'group-2\' }) {\\r\\n  const meaningCheck = groupSection(group, \'Check the meaning, not just the word\');\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    {groupSection(group, group === \'group-1\' ? \'Find the target, then place it\' : \'Find the requirement, then place it\')}\\r\\n    {groupSection(group, \'From sentence to diagram\')}\\r\\n    {group === \'group-1\' && groupSection(group, \'Read the only as a complete expression\')}\\r\\n    {cloneElement(meaningCheck, {}, Children.toArray(meaningCheck.props.children).slice(0, -1))}\\r\\n    <details className=\\"co-practical-note\\"><summary>More sentences to recall and explain</summary>{groupSection(group, \'Say the rule without the clues\')}</details>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction PermissionBoundary() {\\r\\n  const boundary = sections(conditionalReferenceContent().props.children).find(section => section.props[\'data-reference-boundary\'] !== undefined);\\r\\n  if (!boundary) throw new Error(\'Missing approved permission and instruction boundary\');\\r\\n  return <NoteSection title=\\"Keep permission and instructions distinct\\"><p>A conditional can give permission or an instruction. Preserve that strength instead of turning it into a report of what someone did.</p>{Children.toArray(boundary.props.children).slice(3)}</NoteSection>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction ContrapositivePractice() {\\r\\n  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(0);\\r\\n  const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean[]>(() => referencePracticeItems.map(() => false));\\r\\n  return <NoteSection title=\\"Build an original and its contrapositive\\">\\r\\n    <p>For each sentence, identify the indicator and both complete conditions. Choose the original diagram, then its contrapositive. Read both back before checking. If an answer needs revision, inspect the direction, qualifications and negation, then retry.</p>\\r\\n    <p className=\\"co-kicker\\" role=\\"status\\">Sentence {current + 1} of {referencePracticeItems.length}</p>\\r\\n    {referencePracticeItems.map((item, index) => <div key={item.sentence} hidden={current !== index} data-course-practice-item={index + 1}><IntegratedItem item={item} number={index + 1} onChecked={value => setChecked(previous => previous.map((old, itemIndex) => itemIndex === index ? value : old))}/></div>)}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-choices\\"><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === 0} onClick={() => setCurrent(current - 1)}>Previous sentence</button><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === referencePracticeItems.length - 1 || !checked[current]} onClick={() => setCurrent(current + 1)}>Next sentence</button></div>\\r\\n    <p>Moving between sentences keeps your choices and feedback.</p>\\r\\n  </NoteSection>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction Content({ id }: { id: string }) {\\r\\n  switch (id) {\\r\\n    case \'meaning\': return <ReferenceBody number={1} omitTransition/>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient\': return <ReferenceBody number={2} omitTransition/>;\\r\\n    case \'necessary\': return <><ReferenceBody number={4} omitTransition/><ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"You get a bicycle. Does that establish that you won the raffle?\\" options={[\'Yes. Getting a bicycle proves winning.\', \'No. You could get a bicycle without winning.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You made the required result enough to establish winning. The rule does not say winning is the only way to get a bicycle.\', \'You could buy a bicycle or receive one as a gift. Neither possibility breaks the rule, which only tells us what must follow if you win.\']}/></>;\\r\\n    case \'must-arrow\': return <><MustArrowNote/><NoteSection title=\\"Recall enough and required\\"><p>Use these new examples to check the roles and their direction.</p><StudyDeck group=\\"foundation\\"/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient-words\': return <IndicatorNote group=\\"group-1\\"/>;\\r\\n    case \'necessary-words\': return <><IndicatorNote group=\\"group-2\\"/><PermissionBoundary/></>;\\r\\n    case \'whole-meaning\': return <WholeMeaningNote/>;\\r\\n    case \'missing-requirement\': return <><ReferenceBody number={6}/><ReferenceBody number={7} omitTransition/></>;\\r\\n    case \'contrapositive\': return <><ReferenceBody number={9}/><details className=\\"co-practical-note\\"><summary>Practical questions about diagramming</summary><ReferenceBody number={10} omitTransition/></details><NoteSection title=\\"Two possible rooms, one limit\\"><NegativeCaseLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'foundation-practice\': return <FoundationPractice/>;\\r\\n    case \'sufficient-practice\': return <><GroupPractice group=\\"group-1\\"/><NoteSection title=\\"Build a case that proves the limit\\"><CounterexampleLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'mixed-practice\': return <><GroupPractice group=\\"group-2\\"/><NoteSection title=\\"Mix both families without the label\\"><MixedFamilyPractice/></NoteSection><NoteSection title=\\"Keep the rule while the wording changes\\"><RuleComparisonLab/></NoteSection></>;\\r\\n    case \'contrapositive-practice\': return <ContrapositivePractice/>;\\r\\n    default: throw new Error(`Unknown opening course content: ${id}`);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Article body only. Course routes own titles, navigation and completion. */\\r\\nexport function OpeningCourseContent({ id }: { id: string }) {\\r\\n  return <div className=\\"co-opening cr-sequence opening-course-content\\"><Content key={id} id={id}/></div>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n"}'}]

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 2.4 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"e33cf7","wall_time_seconds":2.1564129,"exit_code":1,"original_token_count":5188,"output":"# AGENTS.md\\r\\n\\r\\nThis file is the Codex-facing adapter for this repository. It summarizes the Claude-oriented project guidance from `CLAUDE.md` in a smaller format that is fast for Codex to scan. `CLAUDE.md` remains the fuller source of project knowledge.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Fast Locator\\r\\n\\r\\n- Vault root (the `~/ai-os` directory IS the Obsidian vault): `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os`\\r\\n- Code repo root (this project): `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os/projects/lsatu`\\r\\n- Live vault knowledge: `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os/wiki/` (hubs, voice, business), `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os/students/`, `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os/corpus/`\\r\\n- Pre-2026-07-16 LSATU product knowledge (archived, read-only): `/Users/joshuaf/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/`\\r\\n\\r\\nIf an older note says `~/Documents/Obsidian Vault/...` or `~/Documents/Claude/02_PROJECTS/LSATU`, treat it as stale — the vault was consolidated into `~/ai-os`. Use the absolute paths above.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Project Map\\r\\n\\r\\n- `src/App.tsx`: route registration and top-level app wiring.\\r\\n- `src/pages/`: route-level screens, including the Foyer and admin/teacher surfaces.\\r\\n- `src/components/`: shared UI, including `foyer/`, `inbox/`, and shadcn/ui primitives.\\r\\n- `src/hooks/`: auth, permissions, and shared data hooks.\\r\\n- `src/lib/`: drill, WAJ, gamification, and other product logic.\\r\\n- `src/integrations/supabase/`: generated Supabase client and types. Do not hand-edit generated types.\\r\\n- `supabase/functions/`: Edge Functions.\\r\\n- `supabase/migrations/`: database schema migrations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Stack And Commands\\r\\n\\r\\n- Stack: React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Supabase, TanStack Query.\\r\\n- Package manager: `npm`. `package-lock.json` is canonical. Ignore stray Bun lockfiles.\\r\\n- Dev server: `npm run dev` on port `8080`.\\r\\n- Build: `npm run build`\\r\\n- Lint: `npm run lint`\\r\\n- Test: `npm run test`\\r\\n- Watch tests: `npm run test:watch`\\r\\n- Typecheck: `npm run typecheck`. Required before a push — `vite build` strips types without checking them, so a type error would ship. `.claude/safe-push.sh` gates on it.\\r\\n- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright, `e2e/smoke.spec.ts`).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Working Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep changes small and aligned with existing patterns.\\r\\n- Use TypeScript React function components and the `@/` path alias.\\r\\n- Preserve Lovable-specific plumbing, including the `lovable-tagger` Vite plugin, the PWA setup, and the service-worker guard in `src/main.tsx`.\\r\\n- Do not change app behavior just to satisfy tooling setup.\\r\\n- Do not hardcode secrets or service-role credentials.\\r\\n- Treat Supabase-generated files as generated artifacts, not hand-edited source.\\r\\n- TypeScript strictness is intentionally loose. Do not tighten it without explicit approval.\\r\\n- Keep this adapter aligned with `CLAUDE.md` without duplicating the full project guide. Put durable detail in `CLAUDE.md`; keep shared reference material in `docs/`, `references/`, or `templates/`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Product Constraints\\r\\n\\r\\n- The Foyer is the primary navigation surface. The `GooeyDock` quick-launch row belongs only on `/foyer`.\\r\\n- Inbox is a real 1:1 student-admin messaging system with PDF attachments.\\r\\n- Admin surfaces must stay responsive on desktop and mobile.\\r\\n- Prefer truthful fallbacks over fake buttons, fake analytics, or placeholder behavior.\\r\\n- Onboarding asks for name, not username. Sign-in uses email. The instructor display name is `Joshua`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Smart Drill Note\\r\\n\\r\\nOn `/drill`, adaptive Smart Drill can show a `currentQuestion` that is not the same as `session.questionQueue[session.currentIndex]`. Any per-question UI state must key off `currentQuestion.qid` unless the code path is explicitly limited to queued drills.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verification (must not skip)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Any change to `src/components/` or `src/pages/` is not \\"done\\" until it has been viewed running in the app (dev server + a browser tool), with a screenshot or DOM check as evidence. Never report a UI change complete on the strength of the diff alone. This is the single biggest recurring failure across past sessions — a hard gate, not a suggestion.\\r\\n- **Responsive fixes carry a wider gate: verify across the full emulate matrix BEFORE pushing, not after Joshua reports it.** Narrow, mid, and wide viewports plus the sidecar-docked case, every time. A pushed \\"fix\\" that does not hold costs a second full session; this has already happened once.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Workflow Expectations\\r\\n\\r\\n- Run `npm run build` before wrapping up significant code or documentation work.\\r\\n- If tests are relevant to the change, run them too.\\r\\n- After completing a change, stage the intended files, commit with a concise message, and push to `origin main` unless the user says otherwise.\\r\\n- **Push via `.claude/safe-push.sh`, not raw `git push`.** Lovable auto-commits to `main` mid-session, so a raw push can be rejected or race a concurrent commit. The script fetches, merges `origin/main` if it diverged (never rebases, never force-pushes), then pushes. It also gates on `npm run typecheck`.\\r\\n- **Never roll `main` back.** Do not use Lovable\'s \\"Revert to commit\\", \\"revert and resend\\", or history restore, and never reset or force-push `main`. On 2026-09-27 an accidental \\"revert and resend\\" (b998596) silently undid three merged PRs across 121 question-bank files, and students saw the wrong questions again. To undo your own work, `git revert <your SHA>` only. If a Lovable dialog offers a revert, dismiss it; if one fires, stop and tell Joshua before repairing anything.\\r\\n- Existing Codex repo hooks live in `.codex/hooks.json`; preserve them unless the task explicitly requires a hook change.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Session Protocol (second brain)\\r\\n\\r\\nProduct context, status, and decisions live in the Obsidian vault at `~/ai-os/`, not this repo. Two repo-local skills in `.agents/skills/` run the session ritual; the canonical protocol is in the vault `CLAUDE.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe vault was rebuilt 2026-07-16 (paths relative to `~/ai-os`). Live: teaching voice `wiki/teaching-voice.md` (route ALL student-facing copy through it), the business `wiki/entities/aspiring-attorneys.md`, a student\'s record `students/<name>/` (see `students/README.md`), teaching knowledge `corpus/index.md`, and the `wiki/{tasks,hot,dashboard,index,log}.md` hubs named below. Archived read-only reference (pre-rebuild product knowledge, may be stale): `archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/` — product context `…/synthesis/intro-to-lr-product.md`, design system `…/synthesis/intro-to-lr-design.md`, quality bar `…/synthesis/bootcamp-quality-bar.md`, domain index `…/index.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n- `pickup` — start of session. Read `wiki/tasks.md` (the Now / Next / Done ledger) first, then `wiki/hot.md`, `wiki/dashboard.md`, skim `wiki/index.md`, read the latest `wiki/log.md` entry. Emit a 6-8 line briefing (where we left off, Now, Next, open threads, hot, suggested next) and wait. Do not deep-read other pages until pointed at a task.\\r\\n- `wrapup` — end of session. Propose which `## Now` tasks finished and confirm before writing; a wrong \\"Done\\" is the failure to avoid. Then strike finished items through in `wiki/tasks.md` with a date, refresh `wiki/hot.md`, append a dated `wiki/log.md` entry (newest first, distinct label for same-day sessions), update the task anchor.\\r\\n\\r\\n`wiki/tasks.md` is the single source of truth for what is open vs done. Finished work is struck through so a new session never re-runs it. `raw/` in the vault is immutable.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codex Adapter Layout\\r\\n\\r\\n- `.codex/config.toml`: minimal shared Codex project config. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 0.2 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"a9309a","wall_time_seconds":0.0000191,"exit_code":1,"original_token_count":8839,"output":"  return <div className=\\"cr-sequence\\">\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={1} label=\\"Start with meaning\\" title=\\"What does a conditional tell you?\\">\\r\\n      <p>A <strong>condition</strong> is an idea that can be true or false. You win a raffle. You get a bicycle. We can ask whether either condition holds in a particular case.</p>\\r\\n      <p>A <strong>conditional statement</strong> tells us that if one condition is true, another has to be true too. It gives us a rule we can use, even before we know whether either condition is true in a particular case.</p>\\r\\n      <p className=\\"co-if-inline\\">We aren\'t saying the first condition happened. We\'re asking what would follow <strong>if</strong> it did.</p>\\r\\n      <HypotheticalFigure/>\\r\\n      <h3>Why learn this?</h3><p>On the LSAT, you need to distinguish what the information proves from what it leaves open. A conditional rule can help you prove a conclusion. An argument can also misuse the rule and reach a conclusion it hasn\'t proved. We\'ll practice telling those apart.</p>\\r\\n      <p>Let\'s read one rule.</p><blockquote>{raffleRule}</blockquote>\\r\\n      <p>Under this rule, winning the raffle makes getting a bicycle certain. Winning without getting one would break the stated relationship. That is what we mean by a <strong>guarantee</strong> here.</p>\\r\\n      <p>Compare that with “If you win the raffle, you usually get a bicycle.” Usually allows an exception. Our rule does not. Take the stated rule as given; we are asking what it tells us, not whether a real organizer keeps a promise.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Does the rule itself tell us that you actually win the raffle?\\" options={[\'Yes, it says I win.\', \'No, it tells me what follows if I win.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'You added a case fact. The rule has not reported a win; it tells you what getting one would establish.\', \'Imagining a win helps us understand the rule. We need a separate fact to establish that you actually win.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>Now let\'s take the two conditions one at a time.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={2} label=\\"Sufficient means enough\\" title=\\"One condition gives you enough\\">\\r\\n      <blockquote>{raffleRule}</blockquote><p>The <strong>if-part</strong> is the <strong>sufficient condition</strong>. Knowing you win is enough, under this rule, to know you get a bicycle.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-role-exhibit\\"><span>Sufficient</span><strong>Win the raffle</strong><p>Enough to establish getting a bicycle</p></div>\\r\\n      <p>You might win. You might not. The rule has not settled that question.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"You don\'t win the raffle. Could you still get a bicycle?\\" options={[\'Yes. Getting a bicycle is still possible.\', \'No. Without winning, getting a bicycle is impossible.\']} correct={0} feedback={[\'You could buy one or receive one as a gift. You could also not get one. Neither case creates a winner who fails to get a bicycle, so both fit the rule.\', \'You made winning the only way to get a bicycle. The sentence gives one sufficient condition; it has not excluded other ways.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>Now suppose a fact gives us the sufficient condition. Do we need another fact to establish that you get a bicycle?\\" options={[\'Yes, we need another fact about the bicycle.\', \'No, the rule and the win establish it.\']} correct={1} feedback={[\'The rule already covers the case in which you win. That fact meets its sufficient condition.\', \'Winning meets the sufficient condition. With the rule, that is enough to establish that you get a bicycle.\']}/>\\r\\n      <p>We\'ll now keep this job in mind while changing the wording.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={3} label=\\"The sufficient family\\" title=\\"Different words can preserve the same rule\\">\\r\\n      <p>An <strong>indicator</strong> is an expression that helps you recognize a conditional relationship. These expressions can introduce an idea that is enough to establish another.</p>\\r\\n      <p>For the next examples, use a different stated rule: anyone who borrows a locker has a key. We will express that same connection in several ways. We haven\'t said everyone with a key borrows a locker.</p>\\r\\n      <WordFamily entries={sufficientFamily} role=\\"sufficient\\"/>\\r\\n      <p>When/whenever and any/anytime group related forms together. An ending changes the kind of case being discussed, but these examples keep the same connection. Read the whole sentence. A familiar word is a clue, not a substitute for its meaning.</p>\\r\\n      <ReferenceQuestion prompt=\\"Every guest wearing a blue badge receives a lunch voucher. Keep that qualification with the person.\', \'The voucher is what the rule establishes. It has not said every voucher recipient wears a blue badge.\']}/>\\r\\n      <details className=\\"cr-extension\\"><summary>Two more Group 1 expressions</summary><p><strong>Where</strong> can state a relationship across locations: “Where a collection point operates, parcels can be returned.” An operating collection point establishes the availability of returns there. Understand what the full expression covers before using its group as a placement shortcut.</p></details>\\r\\n      <p>We have seen what can be enough. Now let\'s name what that condition requires.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={4} label=\\"Necessary means required\\" title=\\"The other condition has to be there\\">\\r\\n      <blockquote>{raffleRule}</blockquote><p>The <strong>then-part</strong> is the <strong>necessary condition</strong>. Under this rule, if you win, getting a bicycle has to follow.</p>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-role-exhibit cr-required\\"><span>Necessary</span><strong>Get a bicycle</strong><p>Required whenever you win the raffle</p></div>\\r\\n      <p>Ask “required for what?” Here, a required result of winning under this rule. Next, let\'s see what happens when a requirement is missing.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={6} label=\\"A missing requirement\\" title=\\"What if the requirement is missing?\\" dark>\\r\\n      <ContrapositiveDiscovery/>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={7} label=\\"The four situations\\" title=\\"Keep what follows separate from what stays open\\">\\r\\n      <p>Change the fact about your outcome while keeping the rule. Treat each fact as settled, not as a report that you are still waiting. Its reasoning depends on the missing required result, not on reversing whichever words happen to appear.</p>\\r\\n      <p>We now understand the relationship in words. Symbols will let us record that understanding without carrying every word of the sentence.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={8} label=\\"Build the first diagram\\" title=\\"Give the relationship a shorter form\\">\\r\\n      <p>Put the sufficient condition on the <strong>left</strong>, the necessary condition on the <strong>right</strong>, and a <strong>must arrow</strong> between them.</p>\\r\\n      <RuleDiagram left=\\"Sufficient: enough\\" right=\\"Necessary: required\\"/>\\r\\n      <p>The arrow means the left condition requires the right. We find it by asking what is required, not by taking whichever words come next.</p>\\r\\n      <p>You\'ll work through the less familiar expressions in their Group 1 and Group 2 lessons. Let\'s try all four patterns.</p>\\r\\n      <SignPatterns/>\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-method\\"><p className=\\"co-kicker\\">The complete five-step routine</p><ol><li><strong>Find the indicator.</strong> Read its job in the whole sentence.</li><li><strong>Identify both complete ideas.</strong> Keep restrictions such as current or submitted by Friday.</li><li><strong>Place the roles.</strong> Sufficient goes left; necessary goes right. Choose labels you can read back.</li><li><strong>Write the contrapositive.</strong> Reverse the sides and negate both complete conditions.</li><li><strong>Read both in English.</strong> Compare them with what the original sentence actually requires.</li></ol></div>\\r\\n      <p>The original and its contrapositive describe the same relationship. If writing both helps you see that relationship, write both. If you can read the contrapositive from the original when it is relevant, you needn\'t copy it merely to have a second line.</p>\\r\\n      <p>Read an arrow forward to use its stated direction. To read its contrapositive, start from the right condition\'s absence and work back to the left condition\'s absence. That is a different move from reading the arrow backward unchanged.</p>\\r\\n    </ReferenceStep>\\r\\n\\r\\n    <ReferenceStep number={10} label=\\"Practical diagramming questions\\" title=\\"Use writing to make your reasoning easier to check\\">\\r\\n      <div className=\\"cr-faq\\">\\r\\n        <details><summary>When should I diagram?</summary><p>While learning, write enough to make your choices visible. A difficult sentence, several rules or a connection you keep rereading can be a reason to put the relationship on paper. With practice, you may hold a simple rule mentally. Use the writing to help the reasoning.</p></details>\\r\\n        <details><summary>How do I check whether my diagram is right?</summary><p>Read it back and compare the whole meaning. Did you keep each restriction? Does your arrow promise something the original leaves open? When a diagram is wrong, record the exact phrase and the mistake it produced. That gives you something specific to practice. Familiarity alone is not proof of correctness.</p></details>\\r\\n        <details><summary>What if writing takes time?</summary><p>Start by producing a correct, readable diagram. We\'re checking that you can produce both. Once that skill is reliable, a performance task need not require both lines for every rule.</p></aside>\\r\\n        <details><summary>How should I abbreviate the conditions?</summary><p>Use short labels that bring back the complete idea. Changing the subject changed the rule, even though both sentences contain always.</p></div></div>}\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:755:        <p>We call getting a bicycle the <strong>necessary condition</strong>. Necessary means required. Here it is a required result of winning, not a task you must complete before entering the raffle.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:784:        <ThinkPause prompt=\\"If I get a bicycle, must I have won the raffle?\\">\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:804:        : \\"A necessary condition is something the other condition requires. Group 2 helps us recognize what must be true when that other condition holds. The requirement belongs on the right because the left condition cannot hold without it. Having the requirement, though, leaves the left condition unknown unless something else settles it.\\"}</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:807:      <p>Before looking for a word, ask what the sentence says. Does it give a rule, cover every member of a group, promise a result, or name something required? Each can tell us that if one condition holds, another must hold. A sentence about what usually happens leaves room for exceptions; a conditional rule makes its consequence certain whenever its sufficient condition holds.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:808:      <p>Read the arrow as <strong>must</strong>. The sufficient condition goes on the left. The necessary condition goes on the right. If the left condition is true, the right condition must be true too. The arrow doesn\'t say which event happened first, and it doesn\'t establish that one event caused the other.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:820:        <p>Other sentences promise an outcome: “A silver seal ensures the painting has been inspected” or “A silver seal implies the painting has been inspected.” Here, the promised outcome is inspection. Ensures and implies express the arrow between the two complete ideas. Leads to, will, and always can also express a definite result in a rule, but the word alone doesn\'t settle the meaning. “The studio will open tomorrow” gives us no sufficient condition to put on the left.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:830:        <p>You may also hear the requirement as “In order to borrow a camera, you must have a current membership.” The goal is borrowing; the required condition is membership. Only and only if can set the same restriction. We\'ll work through their wording next.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:832:        <p>You won\'t always see a familiar word. Find what the sentence says is required <strong>for the other condition</strong>. Then check that your arrow keeps that requirement on the right.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:855:        <blockquote>The only people admitted are members.</blockquote>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:856:        <p>The only what? The only people admitted. The complete target is admitted people. If someone is admitted, the sentence tells us they\'re a member.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:858:        <p>A member who stays outside fits this rule. Nothing says every member is admitted. Check that your diagram keeps that possibility open.</p>\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:892:    <figcaption>A conditional tells us what must be true if the first condition is true. It doesn\'t tell us that the first condition actually is true.</figcaption>\\r\\n"}'}]

firstChoice : undefined} type=\\"button\\" key={option} aria-pressed={target === option} onClick={() => change(() => setTarget(option))}>{option}</button>)}</div>\\r\\n    <h3 id={sideQuestion}>Which complete idea goes on the left of the must arrow?</h3>\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-choices\\" role=\\"group\\" aria-labelledby={sideQuestion}>{sideOptions(item, index).map(option => <button type=\\"button\\" key={option} aria-pressed={left === option} onClick={() => change(() => setLeft(option))}>{option}</button>)}</div>\\r\\n    {left && <RuleDiagram left={left} right={left === item.left ? item.right : item.left} label={`Your diagram: ${left} implies ${left === item.left ? item.right : item.left}`}/>}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"cr-control-row\\"><button type=\\"button\\" className=\\"co-primary\\" disabled={target === null || left === null} onClick={() => { setChecked(true); onChecked(true); }}>Check sentence {number}</button><button type=\\"button\\" className=\\"cr-reset\\" onClick={reset}>Try sentence {number} again</button></div>\\r\\n    <div role=\\"status\\">{checked && <div className={`co-feedback ${targetCorrect && sideCorrect ? \'co-correct\' : \'\'}`}>\\r\\n      <strong>{targetCorrect && sideCorrect ? \'Your translation preserves the rule.\' : \'Revise the part described below.\'}</strong>\\r\\n      <p>{targetCorrect ? `You found the complete target: ${item.target}.` : target === item.partial ? item.partialFeedback : item.otherFeedback}</p>\\r\\n      <p>{sideCorrect ? \'Your arrow keeps the direction the sentence gives.\' : item.reversed}</p>\\r\\n      <p>Here, <strong>{item.word}</strong> points to what is {item.family === \'sufficient\' ? \'enough, so its target goes on the left\' : \'required, so its target goes on the right\'}. {item.why}</p>\\r\\n      <p>Read it back: {item.readback}</p>\\r\\n    </div>}</div>\\r\\n  </div>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function MixedFamilyPractice() {\\r\\n  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(0);\\r\\n  const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean[]>(() => mixedFamilyItems.map(() => false));\\r\\n  return <>\\r\\n    <p>These sentences mix both kinds of expression, and nothing tells you which kind is coming. For each one, find the complete idea the expression refers to. Then decide which idea is enough and put it on the left. Check your translation before moving on.</p>\\r\\n    <p className=\\"co-kicker\\" role=\\"status\\">Sentence {current + 1} of {mixedFamilyItems.length}</p>\\r\\n    {mixedFamilyItems.map((item, index) => <div key={item.sentence} hidden={current !== index}><MixedItemCheck item={item} index={index} onChecked={value => setChecked(previous => previous.map((old, itemIndex) => itemIndex === index ? value : old))}/></div>)}\\r\\n    <div className=\\"co-choices\\"><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === 0} onClick={() => setCurrent(current - 1)}>Previous mixed sentence</button><button type=\\"button\\" disabled={current === mixedFamilyItems.length - 1 || !checked[current]} onClick={() => setCurrent(current + 1)}>Next mixed sentence</button></div>\\r\\n    <p>Moving between sentences keeps your choices and feedback.</p>\\r\\n  </>;\\r\\n}\\r\\n"}'}]

## assistant

The opening teaches the core conditional logic correctly. The strongest next improvements are **one permission-wording repair and better final transfer assessment**, not another structural rewrite.

This was a read-only source audit of the nine notes, four labs, imported teaching sections, interactive components and 25 flashcards. I did not run browser checks or tests in this pass.

### Ranked findings

1. **Repair the permission counterexample.**  
   [ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:578](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalOpeningLesson.tsx:578) explains “The only vehicles permitted inside are electric vehicles” using an electric vehicle that “remains outside.” That vehicle might have permission and simply not enter. The explanation shifts from permission to occurrence, weakening the distinction taught elsewhere.  
   **Repair:** “The rule does not promise that every electric vehicle is permitted inside. An electric vehicle that is not permitted inside would still fit the rule.” The main diagram and target are already correct.

2. **Extend the final checkpoint to negative original conditions.**  
   [ConditionalReferenceSequence.tsx:160](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/ConditionalReferenceSequence.tsx:160) supplies six final translation/contrapositive items, all with positive original conditions. Four sign patterns and the film/workshop exercise teach negative conditions correctly, but the final mixed-language checkpoint does not test transfer to a fresh negative original.  
   **Improvement:** preserve all six; add one or two fresh sentences containing a negative sufficient or necessary condition, requiring the learner to negate the **whole condition**.

3. **Add one less-scaffolded translation attempt.**  
   [MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:105](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:105) names the indicator and supplies complete target/diagram choices. Final paired practice also supplies labels and answer choices. These are useful discrimination exercises, but they do not establish that learners can independently identify the expression, construct both labels and explain the direction.  
   **Improvement:** finish with one fresh sentence and a “write or say your translation before revealing” task, followed by a concrete self-check. Treat this as practice, not automatically certified mastery. The existing flashcards already support unscaffolded verbal recall.

4. **Consolidate material-conditional cases explicitly.**  
   This content is **present**, not missing. [CounterexampleLab.tsx:60](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/CounterexampleLab.tsx:60) correctly implements all four configurations and explains each. However, a learner can find the converse counterexample without exploring every configuration. Meanwhile, the “four situations” exercise concerns four starting facts, not four complete truth assignments.  
   **Improvement:** add a compact recap showing three compatible combinations and the single violation: sufficient present, necessary absent. Say “fits this rule,” not “proves the universal rule true.” Formal truth-table terminology is unnecessary here.

5. **Make the mixed lab’s workload easier to perceive.**  
   [OpeningCourseContent.tsx:193](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningCourseContent.tsx:193) and [235](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningCourseContent.tsx:235) combine Group 2 target work, diagram work, a meaning check, six mixed translations and four equivalent-rule comparisons. Each component has a purpose, but this checkpoint has substantially more operations than its neighbors.  
   **Improvement:** retain the content and introduce three clearly named practice rounds with local progress. This is a pacing recommendation, not a correctness defect.

Minor copy: “nothing tells you which kind is coming” at [MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:125](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:125) overstates unpredictability because families alternate deterministically. “The family label is hidden until you check” is exact.
